born.why: The rewrite prioritizes eating confirmed safe fruits for efficiency, avoids known poisons strictly unless starving, and uses innate instincts as a Bayesian prior for unknown fruits, opting to taste when hunger is moderate (to learn) or eat when high (to survive), optimizing the trade-off between learning and survival.
The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately if starving, avoids known poison unless desperate, and efficiently eats confirmed safe fruits while tasting unknown ones to expand knowledge base.

The code prioritizes survival by avoiding known poisons immediately, uses trait-based analogy (smell/shape matching) to assess risk for new fruits, and defaults to tasting only when hunger justifies the risk, preventing unnecessary starvation or poisoning.

The code improves survival by distinguishing between "known poison" (leave), "safe food" (carry to pantry for later when less hungry, or eat if carrying), and "unknown" (taste if safe enough, eat if starving). It leverages shared traits (color, shape, smell) to infer safety of new species faster than relying solely on species keys, reducing unnecessary tasting deaths.

The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately when starvation is imminent, uses a stricter threshold (3 bites) to confirm safety before 'eat', avoids known poison unless starving, and distinguishes between testing new food ('taste') only when safe from hunger, otherwise leaving or eating based on urgency.

The code prioritizes survival by eating only when hunger is critical or safety is strongly confirmed, uses tasting to gather data on new fruits while minimizing risk by avoiding them when not hungry, and avoids known poisons more aggressively than before.
